title: The open–closed sequence for module sheaves over a sheaf of rings
statement:
Let $X$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated, $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ a
quasi-compact open immersion with closed complement $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$,
and $B$ a sheaf of rings on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$, with coefficient rings $j^*B$
on $U$ and $i^*B$ on $Z$. Then:

1. $j^*$ and $j_!$ are exact, $j_!\dashv j^*$, and the unit
$N\to j^*j_!N$ is an isomorphism;
2. $i_*$ is exact, the counit $i^*i_*G\to G$ is an isomorphism (so $i_*$ is
fully faithful), and $j^*i_*=0$;
3. for every $B$-module sheaf $M$ the sequence
$0\to j_!j^*M\to M\to i_*i^*M\to0$, formed by the counit of $j_!\dashv j^*$
and the unit of $i^*\dashv i_*$, is exact;
4. for a morphism $g:X'\to X$ with $X'$ qcqs and base changes
$j':U'\to X'$, $i':Z'\to X'$, $g_U:U'\to U$, $g_Z:Z'\to Z$, there are
canonical isomorphisms $g^*j_!\simeq j'_!g_U^*$, $g^*i_*\simeq i'_*g_Z^*$, and
$g^*$ carries the sequence of (3) for $M$ to the sequence of (3) for $g^*M$.

proof.text: Fix on every scheme over $X$ the coefficient sheaf given by inverse image of $B$. For $f:T\to S$, define $f^*F$ by applying the abelian inverse image to $F$ and to its action: $f^{-1}(B_S\times F)\simeq f^{-1}B_S\times f^{-1}F\to f^{-1}F$. Define $(f_*H)(W)=H(T\times_SW)$, with $B_S$-action through $B_S\to f_*f^{-1}B_S$. The constructions and the finite-product comparison are in [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]; no tensor extension of coefficients is needed because the chosen coefficients are precisely the inverse images. Thus these module functors have the abelian functors as carriers. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful], forgetting actions is faithful and preserves kernels and cokernels. It reflects zero objects, since zero underlying sections give the zero module, and isomorphisms, since the inverse of a bijective linear map is linear. Hence it reflects exactness as well. These constructions do not use commutativity of $B$.

proof.text: Clauses (1),(4) of [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] identify the open site with the slice and give at most one factorization of an object through $U$. In the inverse-image formula [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], for $V\to U$ the pair $(V\to X,\phi:V\xrightarrow{\sim}U\times_XV)$ is initial in $\mathcal I_V$: a map from it to $(W,\psi)$ is uniquely the $X$-map $V\to W$ encoded by $\psi$. It is therefore final in $\mathcal I_V^{\mathrm{op}}$, so the colimit is $F(V\to X)$. These values already form a sheaf because slice coverings are the coverings over $U$. Thus $j^*$, including on $B$, is slice restriction. By [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf], its presheaf extension is $P_N(W)=N(W\to U)$ when $W$ factors through $U$, and zero otherwise, with restricted $B(W)$-action. Define $j_!N=P_N^\#$ using [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]; its carrier is exactly abelian extension by zero.

proof.text: The adjunction $f^{-1}\dashv f_*$ on abelian sheaves restricts to these module categories. Explicitly write $L=f^{-1}$, $R=f_*$, unit $\eta$, and actions $\mu_M,\mu_H$. The action-map calculation below takes place in sheaves of sets; additivity of the maps is already given by the abelian adjunction. An abelian map $a:LM\to H$ has adjunct $b=Ra\circ\eta_M$. The two sides of $a\circ L\mu_M=\mu_H\circ(1\times a)$ have adjuncts $b\circ\mu_M$ and $R\mu_H\circ(\eta_{B_S}\times b)$, respectively: this is naturality of $\eta$ on $B_S\times M$, using its product compatibility. The former equality is $f^{-1}B_S$-linearity of $a$, the latter is $B_S$-linearity of $b$. Thus the hom bijection restricts in both directions, and its unit and counit are exactly the underlying abelian ones. No coefficient commutativity enters these equations.

source.place: Tag 03D3 (lemma-adjoint-push-pull-modules), with the omitted reverse implication supplied by the equality of adjuncts

proof.text: Apply the existing [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] with the commutative coefficient sheaf $\mathbb Z_X$, not with a finite coefficient ring. Abelian sheaves are canonically $\mathbb Z_X$-module sheaves: the integer $n$ acts by repeated addition, and this action extends uniquely to the sheafification of the constant integer presheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Every abelian sheaf map preserves that action. On a scheme $T\to X$, the canonical map $f^{-1}\mathbb Z_X\to\mathbb Z_T$ constructed in [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] lets every abelian sheaf on $T$ carry an $f^{-1}\mathbb Z_X$-action by restriction of its integer action; thus the cited theorem applies to every abelian sheaf on both the open and closed pieces. Its module inverse images with the identified coefficient sheaves have the abelian inverse images as carriers by Steps 1--2. Consequently the cited statement supplies on abelian sheaves the adjunction $j_!\dashv j^*$, exactness of $j_!$ and $i_*$, natural isomorphisms $j^*j_!\simeq1$ and $i^*i_*\simeq1$, the vanishings $j^*i_*=0$ and $i^*j_!=0$, and the canonical short exact sequence $0\to j_!j^*F\to F\to i_*i^*F\to0$. Its hypotheses hold because the complementary open immersion in the item is quasi-compact. This is a use of the cited statement, not a transport of a finite-coefficient proof.

To verify that the particular adjunction maps are invertible, first observe that $i_*$ reflects isomorphisms: applying $i^*$ to $i_*a$ and conjugating by the stated natural isomorphism $i^*i_*\simeq1$ recovers $a$. The localization sequence for $F=i_*G$ and $j^*i_*=0$ show that its unit $\eta_{i,i_*G}$ is invertible. The triangle identity $i_*\varepsilon_{i,G}\circ\eta_{i,i_*G}=1$ makes $i_*\varepsilon_{i,G}$ invertible, hence $\varepsilon_{i,G}$ is invertible. Similarly $j_!$ reflects isomorphisms using $j^*j_!\simeq1$; the sequence for $F=j_!N$ and $i^*j_!=0$ make $\varepsilon_{j,j_!N}$ invertible, and $\varepsilon_{j,j_!N}\circ j_!\eta_{j,N}=1$ gives invertibility of $\eta_{j,N}$. Thus we obtain the actual unit and counit isomorphisms, without interpreting an unspecified functor isomorphism as an adjunction map.

For the open module adjunction, a linear map $P_N\to M$ is determined by its components on objects over $U$, where it is a map $N\to j^*M$; on all other objects its source is zero. Naturality of these components gives the converse map of presheaves. The universal property in [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] therefore gives $\operatorname{Hom}_B(j_!N,M)=\operatorname{Hom}_{j^*B}(N,j^*M)$, with the same underlying abelian unit and counit. The exactness of $j_!$ and the unit isomorphism in clause (1) follow from Steps 4--5 and the forgetful comparison of Step 1. Moreover every inverse image $f^*$ with these inverse-image coefficients is exact: its underlying abelian functor is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-site-pullback-abelian-exact]. This proves the remaining assertion about $j^*$ and will also apply to $i^*,g^*,i'^*,j'^*$.

By Steps 1--5, exactness of $i_*$, invertibility of its counit, and $j^*i_*=0$ in clause (2) hold for $B$-modules. The counit is the module counit by Step 3. For full faithfulness, the bijections $\operatorname{Hom}_B(i_*G,i_*H)=\operatorname{Hom}_{i^*B}(i^*i_*G,H)=\operatorname{Hom}_{i^*B}(G,H)$ identify the forward map with $i_*$ by the triangle identity. Likewise the two module maps in clause (3) forget to exactly the counit and unit of the abelian sequence of Step 4, so that sequence is exact for $B$-modules. We will use the resulting detection criterion: if $j^*F=i^*F=0$ then this sequence gives $F=0$; if a morphism becomes invertible under both restrictions, exactness of the restrictions makes its kernel and cokernel have zero restrictions, so they vanish and the morphism is invertible.

For clause (4), the base changes $j'$ and $i'$ are open and closed immersions by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change], and $j'$ is quasi-compact by [lem-pc-quasi-compact-base-change]. They are complementary: the open is $g^{-1}(U)$ and the closed fibre has support $g^{-1}(|Z|)$ (affine locally it is cut out by the image of the ideal of $Z$). Thus Steps 1--7 apply also on $X'$. Composition of the site inverse images has its canonical adjunction-compatible identification by [lem-weil-pbc-site-morphism-composition]. Indeed direct image along a composite evaluates to $H(T\times_SW)$ by associativity of fibre products, using [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. These identifications lift to our module categories by the action construction in Step 1. We henceforth use $i'^*g^*\simeq g_Z^*i^*$ and $j'^*g^*\simeq g_U^*j^*$, with these specified identifications on coefficient sheaves as well.

proof.text: Open base change is a direct adjunction calculation. On an object $W\to U$, both $(j^*g_*H)(W)$ and $(g_{U*}j'^*H)(W)$ equal $H(X'\times_XW)$, with the same coefficient action and restrictions. Consequently there are natural bijections $\operatorname{Hom}(g^*j_!N,H)=\operatorname{Hom}(N,j^*g_*H)=\operatorname{Hom}(N,g_{U*}j'^*H)=\operatorname{Hom}(j'_!g_U^*N,H)$. The isomorphism $\alpha_N:g^*j_!N\xrightarrow{\sim}j'_!g_U^*N$ is the one corresponding to identity maps under this hom identification: applying it to the identity on either represented object gives inverse maps because the bijections are natural. This proves the first canonical isomorphism. The sectionwise direct-image equality used here is valid for arbitrary $g$.

source.place: Current blueprint proof part (4), open base change; adjunction argument made explicit using sectionwise direct image

proof.text: Let $\varepsilon_i:i^*i_*\to1$ be the closed counit. Define the canonical closed comparison $\beta_G:g^*i_*G\to i'_*g_Z^*G$ as the $i'^*\dashv i'_*$ adjunct of $i'^*g^*i_*G\simeq g_Z^*i^*i_*G\xrightarrow{g_Z^*\varepsilon_{i,G}}g_Z^*G$. After $j'^*$ its source and target vanish, since $j'^*g^*i_*G\simeq g_U^*j^*i_*G=0$ and $j'^*i'_*=0$. Its closed restriction satisfies $\varepsilon_{i',g_Z^*G}\circ i'^*\beta_G=g_Z^*\varepsilon_{i,G}$ under the composition identification. Both counits are isomorphisms by clause (2), so $i'^*\beta_G$ is an isomorphism. Detection from Step 7 on $X'$ proves that $\beta_G$ is an isomorphism. This uses the composition theorem [lem-weil-pbc-site-morphism-composition], not a base-change theorem restricted to weakly etale $g$.

proof.text:
Finally these isomorphisms identify the actual sequence maps. Put $\delta_M:j'^*g^*M\simeq g_U^*j^*M$ and $\gamma_M:i'^*g^*M\simeq g_Z^*i^*M$. For the open map, put $N=j^*M$ and use the composite adjunction bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{X'}(g^*j_!N,g^*M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{U}(N,j^*g_*g^*M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{U}(N,g_{U*}j'^*g^*M)$. Under this bijection both $g^*\varepsilon_{j,M}$ and $\varepsilon_{j',g^*M}\circ j'_!(\delta_M^{-1})\circ\alpha_{j^*M}$ correspond to
$N\xrightarrow{\eta^{g_U}_N}g_{U*}g_U^*N\xrightarrow{g_{U*}(\delta_M^{-1})}g_{U*}j'^*g^*M$, by the two triangle identities and the defining adjunction property of $\alpha$. Hence the open maps agree. For the closed map, the $i'^*$-adjunct of $\beta_{i^*M}\circ g^*\eta_{i,M}$ is the composite $i'^*g^*M\xrightarrow{\gamma_M}g_Z^*i^*M\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}g_Z^*i^*M$: the counit equation for $\beta$ reduces it to $g_Z^*(\varepsilon_{i,i^*M}\circ i^*\eta_{i,M})=\mathrm{id}$ by the triangle identity. This is also the adjunct of $i'_*(\gamma_M)\circ\eta_{i',g^*M}$, so those two maps agree. Thus the pulled-back counit and unit are exactly the new counit and unit. Exactness of $g^*$ from Step 6 now sends the sequence of clause (3) to that for $g^*M$, as asserted.
